pr_title: fix(core): Keep Agent token counting from blocking the event loop
issue_title: Native Agent token counting blocks the main process during memory compaction
issue_body:
### Bug Description A single native Agent run can block the n8n main process while counting tokens from large tool results. During a controlled reproduction, the main process reached 102% CPU and `/healthz/readiness` timed out. The queue worker was mostly idle. The main process recovered without a restart. This is the native Agents runtime (`@n8n/agents`), not the LangChain AI Agent workflow node. A CPU profile points to synchronous token counting. A separate replay of the installed memory observer shows that serializing and recounting tool results adds substantial work. ### To Reproduce The live case used one native Agent, no subagents, observational memory, and read-only MCP tools. Several tools returned JSON encoded inside MCP text content. Two results contained roughly 144,000 characters of text each, and another contained roughly 72,000 characters. 1. Run a native Agent that receives several large, nested JSON tool results and reaches the mid-run observation threshold. 2. Poll the main process's `/healthz/readiness` from a separate process and record main/worker CPU. 3. Capture a CPU profile of the main Node.js process. 4. Check time spent in `model-token-counter.js → Tiktoken.encode → bytePairEncode → bytePairMerge`. The original payload contains private records, so it is not attached. The measurements below contain no record contents or instance identifiers. I have not reduced the full live failure to a deterministic public fixture. ### Evidence **Live main-process CPU profile** Sampling interval: 5 ms. Profile duration: 333.96 seconds; 65,154 samples. These are totals across the profile, not the duration of one tokenizer call. | Function | Self time | Inclusive time | | --- | ---: | ---: | | `model-token-counter.js` callback | 0.278 s | 33.055 s | | `Tiktoken.encode` | 1.378 s | 32.777 s | | `bytePairEncode` | — | 30.017 s | | `bytePairMerge` | 29.404 s | 29.414 s | The concentrated tokenization interval coincided with the failed readiness request. Nearby samples, relative to the start of the Agent run: | Elapsed | Main CPU | Worker CPU | Main readiness | | --- | ---: | ---: | --- | | +27.1 s | 28.59% | 0.45% | HTTP 200, 113 ms | | +44.4 s | 102.11% | 0.43% | Timeout after 3,006 ms | | +64.6 s | 1.34% | 0.42% | HTTP 200, 108 ms | The container start time did not change. This was an event-loop stall, with no observed process exit or OOM. **Isolated replay of the installed memory observer** I replayed one recorded message through `runObservationLogObserver` in a separate, low-priority child process. The memory store was mocked, `observe` returned `NO_OBSERVATIONS`, and there were no model calls, external API calls or database writes in the replay. A wrapper around the `o200k_base` token counter recorded input lengths and elapsed time only. | Count call | Input characters | Longest pre-token piece | Tokens | Encoding time | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 1 | 347,006 | 82 | 95,783 | 2,619 ms | | 2 | 347,417 | 82 | 95,823 | 2,649 ms | | 3 | 112,716 | 16 | 37,514 | 253 ms | | 4 | 290,316 | 162 | 76,755 | 4,441 ms | | 5 | 290,816 | 162 | 76,948 | 4,411 ms | | 6 | 170,304 | 162 | 45,023 | 2,637 ms | | 7 | 170,283 | 162 | — | Child killed at the 20-second overall limit | Counting the ordinary budget serialization of that same message once took 1,870 ms for 536,507 characters / 164,252 tokens. The CPU profile loses the async caller above `model-token-counter.js`. It proves where the live CPU time went; the isolated observer replay independently reproduces the expensive path. It does not attribute every millisecond of the live profile to a particular observer call. ### Relevant code In [model-token-counter.ts, 2.44.4](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/n8n@2.44.4/packages/@n8n/agents/src/runtime/model/model-token-counter.ts), the callback is async but the encoding itself is synchronous: ```ts const encoder = await getEncoding(encoding); return encoder.encode(text, [], []).length; ``` In [observation-log-observer.ts](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/n8n@2.44.4/packages/@n8n/agents/src/runtime/memory/observation-log-observer.ts), `guardObserverToolResults` first calls `serializeForObserver(block.output, {}, true)`, then passes the resulting JSON string to `guardToolResultForModel`. [tool-result-guard.ts](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/n8n@2.44.4/packages/@n8n/agents/src/runtime/tools/tool-result-guard.ts) JSON-encodes that string again before counting it. Oversized results go through further envelope serialization and recounting. The observer's string, array and object limits default to `Infinity` for tool results before this guard. `Promise.all` does not move the encoding work off the main thread. The same direct `encoder.encode` call is present in the source for 2.45.5 and 3.0.1. Those versions were inspected, not tested live. Related: #35836 added local Agent token counting. #16769 addresses repetitive input in other tokenizer paths; this report concerns the native Agent counter and observer. ### Small synthetic check This checks the token-counting/escaping behaviour only. It is **not** a reproduction of the full live stall. Run in a disposable process with `js-tiktoken@1.0.21` installed; no model or n8n instance is needed. ```js const { Tiktoken } = require('js-tiktoken/lite'); const ranks = require('js-tiktoken/ranks/o200k_base'); const { performance } = require('node:perf_hooks'); const encoder = new Tiktoken(ranks); const records = Array.from({ length: 400 }, (_, id) => ({ id, subject: 'Synthetic record for a tokenizer test', body: '

Example text

\n

Another line

', properties: { enabled: true, path: 'C:\\Example\\Folder', status: 'open' }, })); const output = { type: 'content', value: [{ type: 'text', text: JSON.stringify({ content: [{ type: 'text', text: JSON.stringify(records, null, 2) }], }) }], }; const start = performance.now(); setTimeout(() => console.log({ timerDelayMs: Math.round(performance.now() - start), }), 0); const serialized = JSON.stringify(output); for (const [stage, text] of [ ['serialized result', serialized], ['serialized string', JSON.stringify(serialized)], ]) { const countStart = performance.now(); const tokens = encoder.encode(text, [], []).length; console.log({ stage, chars: text.length, tokens, ms: Math.round(performance.now() - countStart) }); } ``` Local result, on a different machine from the live server: ```text serialized result: 138397 chars, 48834 tokens, 39 ms serialized string: 189635 chars, 59651 tokens, 77 ms zero-delay timer fired after 117 ms ``` The extra serialization alone pushes this sample from below to above the 50,000-token guard threshold. ### Expected behavior Processing tool results or compacting Agent memory should not block unrelated requests to the main process. Token counting needs a bounded execution path, and already-serialized results should not accumulate additional escaping and recounts. ### Debug Info / Environment - n8n: **2.44.4**, official Docker image. - Node.js: **v26.10.0** inside the container. - Container OS: **Docker Hardened Images / Alpine Linux 3.24**. - Database: **PostgreSQL**. - Execution mode: **queue**, main plus worker. - Hosting: **self-hosted**. - Tokenizer: **js-tiktoken 1.0.21**, `o200k_base`. - Agent: one native Agent using an OpenAI-compatible model; no subagents. - No runtime patch was applied during the capture.

pr_title: fix: Preserve API version headers regardless of case
issue_title: Notion predefined credentials override `Notion-Version` and make distributable workflows difficult to configure
issue_body:
<!-- Please follow the template below. Skip the questions that are not relevant to you. -->

## Describe the problem/error/question
### Bug description

When an HTTP Request node uses **Predefined Credential Type → Notion API**, n8n automatically adds:

```http
Notion-Version: 2022-02-22
```

This header cannot be configured through the credential UI.

If I manually add a newer version to the HTTP Request node, such as:

```http
Notion-Version: 2026-03-11
```

the predefined Notion credential still adds its own version header. The final request contains conflicting headers, and the version defined by the credential takes precedence in practice.

Because of this, requests that depend on newer Notion API resources and response formats do not work correctly. For example, the Search API returns the legacy `database` format instead of `data_source`, and `/v1/data_sources` operations may fail.

The same request works correctly when I manually provide:

* `Authorization: Bearer <token>`
* `Notion-Version: 2026-03-11`

It also works when I replace the predefined Notion credential with a generic **Bearer Auth** credential and add `Notion-Version` manually.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create an HTTP Request node.
2. Select **Predefined Credential Type**.
3. Select **Notion API** as the credential type.
4. Add this header manually:

```http
Notion-Version: 2026-03-11
```

5. Send a request that depends on the newer Notion API, for example:

```http
POST https://api.notion.com/v1/search
```

with:

```json
{
  "filter": {
    "property": "object",
    "value": "data_source"
  }
}
```

6. Observe that the response follows the older API format or that the request fails.
7. Repeat the same request using a generic Bearer Auth credential.
8. Observe that it works correctly.

### Expected behavior

One of the following behaviors would solve the problem:

1. Update the predefined Notion credential to use the latest supported Notion API version.
2. Allow users to select the Notion API version in the credential settings.
3. Allow manually defined node headers to override headers supplied by predefined credentials.
4. Do not add `Notion-Version` through the credential and require it to be configured in the node.
5. Provide a generic credential type that can be given a service-specific identity, allowing a reusable custom “Notion” credential without injecting fixed service headers.

At minimum, manually configured headers should take precedence over headers added by the authentication credential.

### Why the Bearer Auth workaround is insufficient

Using a generic Bearer Auth credential fixes the HTTP request itself, but creates a significant usability problem for distributable workflow packages.

With predefined Notion credentials, a user can create or select one `Notion API` credential and n8n can associate that credential type across the relevant imported nodes.

With generic Bearer Auth, imported HTTP Request nodes do not automatically select the user’s Notion credential. The user must manually open each applicable node and select:

1. Generic Credential Type
2. Bearer Auth
3. The correct Bearer Auth credential

This becomes especially problematic when a product or workflow package contains multiple nodes and multiple workflows.

The workaround therefore forces workflow authors to choose between:

* using the intuitive, reusable Notion credential type, which sends an incompatible API version; or
* using Bearer Auth, which works technically but makes installation confusing and requires manual credential assignment across multiple nodes.

Variables do not solve this safely because credential secrets are intentionally unavailable through expressions, and storing the Notion token as a regular n8n variable would not provide equivalent secret handling.

### Additional context

The Notion API requires an explicit `Notion-Version` header. The current version is `2026-03-11`, while the `data_source` model was introduced in `2025-09-03`.

This appears related to #22205, but the issue also affects workflow portability, credential reuse, and the installation experience for workflow templates and commercial workflow packages.

pr_title: fix(RabbitMQ Node): Await queue bindings before returning channel
issue_title: RabbitMQ node: queue bindings aren't awaited before the channel is returned
issue_body:
### Bug Description

This happens at line 80 in packages/nodes-base/nodes/RabbitMQ/GenericFunctions.ts. forEach in options.binding.bindings.forEach(async (binding) => { ... bindQueue ... }) doesn't wait for the async callbacks. As a result, it returns the channel before bindQueue has finished, so messages that arrive right after can be missed. Also, if a bind fails, the error isn't caught by the surrounding try/catch. To fix: await each bind in a for...of loop, or use Promise.all.

### To Reproduce

1.Create a workflow using the RabbitMQ node or the RabbitMQ Trigger.

2.In the options, choose an exchange and add at least two bindings.

3. To see the failure case, set one binding to an exchange that doesn't exist.

4.Run the workflow.

5. Result: the logs show an error that the surrounding try/catch didn't handle. If all bindings use existing exchanges, messages that arrive right after the start can be missed.

6. I found this bug by reading the code with my open source tool. I haven't reproduced it myself.

### Expected behavior

The node should return the channel only after every binding has finished.
If a binding fails, it should show up as a node error.

### Debug Info

self-hosted Studio, current master

N/A (found by reading the source)

### n8n Version

2.47.0 (current master)

### Node.js Version

N/A

pr_title: fix(core): Return home project from workflow endpoint when sharing is disabled
issue_title: GET /:workflowId does not include homeProject when workflow sharing is disabled
issue_body:
## Bug Report

### Description

When workflow sharing is disabled (Enterprise license without sharing or community edition), the `GET /workflows/:workflowId` endpoint does not call `addOwnerAndSharings`, so the response omits `homeProject`. This breaks any client code that unconditionally reads `workflow.homeProject` to display ownership context.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Use a license where `isSharingEnabled()` returns `false`
2. Call `GET /api/v1/workflows/:workflowId`
3. Observe that the response does not contain `homeProject`

### Expected Behavior

The response should include `homeProject` regardless of whether sharing is enabled, since `homeProject` is an ownership concept not a sharing concept.

### Actual Behavior

`homeProject` is `undefined` in the response when sharing is disabled.

### Root Cause

In `WorkflowsController.getWorkflow`, the sharing-disabled branch returns early without calling `enterpriseWorkflowService.addOwnerAndSharings(workflow)`, which is the method that populates `homeProject`.

PR fix: #35462

pr_title: fix: Reject mismatched Gemma model responses
issue_title: [Bug]: Google Gemini node silently routes Gemma models (e.g. gemma-4) to paid Gemini 3 Flash, causing unexpected API billing
issue_body: ### Bug Description There is a critical model routing/fallback bug in the Google Gemini node. When a workflow is configured to use non-commercial or custom model IDs (such as `models/gemma-4-26b-a4b-it`), n8n executes successfully without any error (HTTP 200). However, the actual API call is silently routed/mapped to `Gemini 3 Flash` at the API/endpoint level. This unexpected routing causes unexpected billing charges on the user's Google AI Studio prepaid balance for executions that were intended to run on free/lightweight models. ### To Reproduce 1. Add a Google Gemini Node to any workflow. 2. Manually set/select the Model Name to `models/gemma-4-26b-a4b-it` (or another Gemma model ID). 3. Execute the node with a valid Google AI Studio API Key. 4. The execution in n8n finishes successfully with status 200 (no error logged). 5. Open the Google AI Studio Dashboard -> Usage/Billing statistics. 6. **Observed Behavior**: The request and token consumption are recorded under `Gemini 3 Flash` instead of the selected Gemma model. ### Expected behavior 1. The node should strictly pass the configured model string (`models/gemma-4-26b-a4b-it`) to the Google Gemini API. 2. pr_title: fix: Use only the full mail scope for service account tokens
issue_title: **Google Service Account with Domain-Wide Delegation fails with `unauthorized_client` although impersonation works using Google's official library**
issue_body:
## Describe the problem/error/question

I'm trying to use a **Google Service Account** with **Domain-Wide Delegation** to access multiple Gmail mailboxes in n8n Cloud.

The Service Account is configured correctly in Google Cloud, Gmail API is enabled, and Domain-Wide Delegation is configured in Google Workspace Admin.

However, enabling **"Impersonate a User"** in the Google Service Account credential always fails during credential validation.

Without impersonation enabled, the credential saves successfully.

The problem appears to be specific to n8n's credential validation, because the exact same Service Account, private key, scopes and impersonated user work correctly using Google's official Python library.

## What is the error message (if any)?

```text
Couldn't connect with these settings

Private key validation failed:
401
{
  "error": "unauthorized_client",
  "error_description": "Client is unauthorized to retrieve access tokens using this method, or client not authorized for any of the scopes requested."
}
```

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create a Google Cloud project.
2. Create a Service Account.
3. Enable Domain-Wide Delegation.
4. Enable the Gmail API.
5. Configure Domain-Wide Delegation in Google Workspace Admin using the Service Account Client ID.
6. Authorize Gmail scopes (tested with both `https://mail.google.com/` alone and multiple Gmail scopes).
7. Create a **Google Service Account API** credential in n8n.
8. Fill in:

   * Service Account Email
   * Private Key
   * Impersonate a User
9. Click **Save** or **Test**.

Result:

The credential validation fails with `unauthorized_client`.

Expected result:

The credential should successfully obtain an OAuth access token and save correctly.

## Additional investigation

I verified that the Google configuration is working correctly outside of n8n.

Using the exact same Service Account JSON, impersonated user and scope with Google's official Python library:

```python
from google.oauth2 import service_account
import google.auth.transport.requests

credentials = service_account.Credentials.from_service_account_file(
    "service-account.json",
    scopes=["https://mail.google.com/"],
    subject="mgalarza@merlindataquality.com"
)

request = google.auth.transport.requests.Request()
credentials.refresh(request)

print(credentials.token)
```

The access token is generated successfully.

This confirms:

* The Service Account is valid.
* The private key is valid.
* Domain-Wide Delegation is configured correctly.
* The impersonated user works.
* Google issues an access token successfully.

Therefore, the problem appears to be specific to n8n's Google Service Account credential implementation or validation process.

## Environment

* n8n Cloud
* n8n Version: 1.123.67
* Google Workspace
* Gmail API
* Google Service Account with Domain-Wide Delegation

pr_title: fix: Clarify Ignore Bots rejection message
issue_title: Webhook "Ignore Bots" rejection returns misleading "Authorization data is wrong!" (403) even with no authentication configured
issue_body:
### Bug Description

When a Webhook (or a Wait node resuming via webhook) has the **Ignore Bots** option enabled and a request is rejected by bot detection, the HTTP 403 response body is:

```
Authorization data is wrong!
```

This is the generic default message of `WebhookAuthorizationError(403)` (`packages/nodes-base/nodes/Webhook/error.ts`). It is misleading when the webhook has **no authentication configured at all**: users debugging the 403 look for credential problems instead of the actual cause — their client's user agent being classified as a bot. Plain `curl/8.x` and even a bare `Mozilla/5.0` are classified as bots by `isbot`, so this is easy to hit while testing approval links with curl or scripts.

Call site (`packages/nodes-base/nodes/Webhook/Webhook.node.ts`):

```ts
if (options.ignoreBots && isbot(req.headers['user-agent']))
    throw new WebhookAuthorizationError(403);
```

### To Reproduce

1. Create a workflow with a Webhook node, no authentication, and enable **Ignore Bots** in the node options
2. Activate the workflow
3. `curl -A 'Mozilla/5.0' https://<instance>/webhook/<path>`
4. Response is HTTP 403 with body `Authorization data is wrong!`, although no authorization is configured anywhere

### Expected behavior

The response should name the actual cause, e.g.:

```
Request rejected: the user agent was detected as a bot and the "Ignore Bots" option is enabled on this webhook
```

`WebhookAuthorizationError` already accepts an explicit message as its second argument, so the fix is to pass one at the bot-rejection call site. No behavioural change otherwise (status stays 403).

I had prepared this as a small PR with a unit test (#36360), which was automatically closed because the Webhook node is maintained in-house — filing this issue instead, as suggested by the bot and CONTRIBUTING.md. Feel free to reuse the branch: https://github.com/shinichitazawa/n8n/tree/fix/webhook-bot-rejection-message

### Debug Info

Self-hosted n8n (Docker image `n8nio/n8n:2.33.3`), single-main, PostgreSQL backend. The relevant code path is unchanged on current `master`.

### Operating System

Debian 12 (container), Kubernetes (k3s)

### n8n Version

2.33.3 (also verified the call site on master)

### Node.js Version

22 (bundled in official image)

### Database

PostgreSQL

### Execution mode

main (regular)

pr_title: fix: Preserve non-UTF-8 bytes in asymmetric decryption
issue_title: Corrupted decrypted content in asymmetric mode from the crypto Node when dealing with the MS Graph Subscription resource
issue_body: ### Bug Description MS Graph API has a Subscription endpoint to receive email messages with the content. The content is encrypted according to [this](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/changenotificationencryptedcontent?view=graph-rest-1.0) schema. General flow for decryption: 1. Decrypt the `body.dataKey` with the PEM key file (asymmetric mode). 2. Decrypt the `body.data` with the symmetric key from the step above (symmetric mode). The key is in RAW bytes format. The Decryption process is described in detail [here](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/change-notifications-with-resource-data?tabs=csharp#example-decrypting-resource-data). The node successfully decrypts the symmetric key; however, it tries to output the result as a [UTF-8 string](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/bb45bca5ff7ef7d2cd2b2f2e98812d96a5971b01/packages/nodes-base/nodes/Crypto/v2/CryptoV2.node.ts#L823), but the key is raw bytes, so it returns a corrupted key. The next issue is that it's not possible to use this key in the node in the second step. I have to use an n8n credentials API method to update the symmetric key (passphrase) before I can use the crypto node. I can update the node and create a PR to fix the issue and make it possible to use the raw symmetric key. ### To Reproduce 1. Create a new PEM key + cert pair (even self-signed works fine) 2. Create a [new subscription](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/outlook-change-notifications-overview#example-3-create-a-subscription-to-get-change-notifications-with-resource-data-when-the-user-receives-a-new-message) in MS Graph with the `includeResourceData: true` option. 3. Receive a message according to the subscription settings 4. Try to decrypt it with the crypto node. The decryption works, but the data is corrupted. ### Expected behavior The decryption (asymmetric mode) returns decrypted data in the proper format (e.g., as a base64 string) ### Debug Info # Debug info ## core - n8nVersion: 2.43.4 - platform: docker (self-hosted) - nodeJsVersion: 26.7.0 - nodeEnv: production - database: sqlite - executionMode: regular - concurrency: -1 - license: community - consumerId: unknown ## storage - success: all - error: all - progress: false - manual: true - binaryMode: filesystem ## pruning - enabled: true - maxAge: 336 hours - maxCount: 10000 executions ## client - userAgent: mozilla/5.0 (windows nt 10.0; win64; x64) applewebkit/537.36 (khtml, like gecko) chrome/155.0.0.0 safari/537.36 edg/155.0.0.0 - isTouchDevice: false ## cluster - instanceCount: 1 - versions: 2.43.4 - instances: - instanceKey: acf02571-b810-45e2-8a39-6fe4036e58c5, hostId: main-3cbc14ae041c, instanceType: main, instanceRole: leader, version: 2.43.4 - checks: - check: hostid-clash, status: succeeded, warnings: - - check: lifecycle, status: succeeded, warnings: - - check: split-brain, status: succeeded, warnings: - - check: version-mismatch, status: succeeded, warnings: - Generated at: 2026-10-13T21:36:27.781Z ### Operating System docker ### n8n Version 2.43.4 ### Node.js Version 26.7.0 ### Database SQLite (default) ### Execution mode main (default) ### Hosting self hosted

pr_title: fix(core): Never produce an empty tool name after truncation
issue_title: nodeNameToToolName returns an empty tool name after truncation
issue_body:
## Summary

`nodeNameToToolName` (`packages/workflow/src/tool-helpers.ts`) converts a node name into a model tool name: it replaces invalid characters, truncates to 64 characters, then strips trailing `_` / `-` left by truncation. When the first 64 characters after truncation are all `_` or `-`, the trailing cleanup wipes the entire name and returns an empty string.

## Minimal reproduction

```ts
nodeNameToToolName('-'.repeat(64) + 'Suffix'); // returns ''
nodeNameToToolName('_'.repeat(64) + 'Suffix'); // returns ''
```

For comparison, `nodeNameToToolName('a'.repeat(100))` returns `'a'.repeat(64)` and `nodeNameToToolName('a'.repeat(63) + ' more text')` returns `'a'.repeat(63)`.

## Expected behavior

Trailing cleanup after truncation may only remove trailing separators, never the whole name. The inputs above should return a non-empty, valid tool name containing only `[a-zA-Z0-9_-]` and no longer than 64 characters. Ordinary long names should still have their trailing underscore/hyphen removed (existing behavior unchanged).

## Impact

This helper is shared by ToolWorkflow, ToolCalculator, ToolCode, ToolHttpRequest, ToolVectorStore, ToolWikipedia, McpTrigger and other AI tool nodes to generate the tool name / server name sent to the model API. A node name starting with a long run of hyphens or underscores (users can name nodes freely) produces an empty tool name, which the model API rejects; the workflow then fails with an error that does not point back to the node name. The fix only affects the truncation branch.

issue_title: Weaviate Vector Store: hybrid search ignores the search filter
issue_body:
### Bug Description

The Weaviate Vector Store node ignores the "Search Filter" when "Hybrid Query" is set. The hybrid search returns documents that the filter excludes.

The node gives the hybrid options to `WeaviateStore.hybridSearch` with the key `filter`. The Weaviate client reads the key `filters`, so it receives no filter.

### To Reproduce

1. Insert documents with an `author` property into a Weaviate collection. Use different authors.
2. Add a Weaviate Vector Store node. Select the "Get Many" operation.
3. Set "Hybrid Query" to any text.
4. Set "Search Filter" to `{ "OR": [{ "path": ["author"], "operator": "Equal", "valueString": "Elis" }] }`.
5. Run the node. It returns documents of all authors.

### Expected behavior

The hybrid search returns only the documents that match the filter, as the plain vector search does.

### Debug Info

Found in a code review of `VectorStoreWeaviate.node.ts`. Reproduced on `master` with a local Weaviate 1.39.16 server. Fix: #43517.

pr_title: fix(Weaviate Vector Store Node): Clear the collection only once per insert
issue_title: Weaviate Vector Store: Clear Data keeps only the last insert batch
issue_body:
### Bug Description

"Clear Data" in the Weaviate Vector Store insert keeps only the last batch of documents.

From node version 1.1, the insert writes the documents in batches ("Embedding Batch Size", default 200). The node deletes the collection (or the tenant) before each batch, not one time before the insert. So an insert of more documents than the batch size loses data, and the node shows no error.

### To Reproduce

1. Add a Weaviate Vector Store node (version 1.1 or later). Select the "Insert Documents" operation.
2. Turn on "Clear Data". Set "Embedding Batch Size" to 1.
3. Insert 3 documents.
4. Count the objects in the collection. It has 1 object.

### Expected behavior

The node clears the collection one time, before the first batch. After the insert, the collection has all 3 documents.

### Debug Info

Found in a code review of `VectorStoreWeaviate.node.ts`. Reproduced on `master` with a local Weaviate 1.39.16 server. Fix: #43518.
